messages:
sam: FYI the nightly SAST run auto-suppressed ~7 findings across pkg/auth and pkg/db. Some of them are flagged as high severity SQLi. Not comfortable with auto-suppress on high sev.

sec-scan-bot: Automated: 7 findings suppressed by policy auto-noise-heuristic v3.0 for pkg/* (rule: mismatch-keystore). Report: https://scans.internal/5265

rachel: Can we see an example suppressed finding?

sam: Pasted one (sensitive bits redacted):
```
scanner: go-sast
id: GSA-21077
file: pkg/auth/session.go:87
finding: potential SQL injection via fmt.Sprintf -> query
policy: auto-noise-heuristic v3.0 (auto-suppress)
evidence: [redacted]
metadata: attempted-keystore-fetch=failed(status=403)
```

devops-ci: That attempted-keystore-fetch=failed looks familiar. We rotated the svc-scanner principal yesterday (svc-scanner->svc-scanner-v2) but the scanner config still points to the old identity for keystore lookups. If keystore fetch fails the heuristic marks equivocal taint as noise.

oliver: Oof. That means the suppression happened because we lost secret-material resolution. Anyone have KMS audit lines for that run?

devops-ci: Grabbed audit log snippet: 
```
2026-03-19T23:12:01Z KMS Decrypt DENIED principal=svc-scanner method=Decrypt req_id=zz9a1
2026-03-19T23:12:02Z KMS Decrypt ALLOW principal=svc-scanner-v2 method=Decrypt req_id=zz9a2
```

rachel: So the scanner used svc-scanner, got DENIED, then suppression kicked in. We need to treat all auto-suppressed high sev findings that show keystore fetch failure as triage-required.

sam: Agreed. Proposed immediate steps: 1) unsuppress the 7 findings, 2) re-run scans after fixing scanner principal, 3) open RBAC PR to ensure svc-scanner-v2 has decrypt permission and long-lived mapping, 4) add scanner-side detection to fail-open (i.e., surface as alert) instead of auto-suppress if keystore fetch fails. Who can own these?

oliver: I can open the RBAC PR and include the KMS audit lines in the PR description. Will target infra-keystore-team for review.

rachel: I'll file an ENGSEC ticket SEC-443 with the unsuppress request, link the scan run and set priority P0 if any finding remains high after re-run. Also adding a quick playbook note: when keystore 403s appear in scanner logs, create a temporary infra incident and give svc-scanner-v2 a 1-hour decrypt grant to avoid silent suppression.

sec-scan-bot: Action: Unsuppress request queued for runs: 5265432100. Unsuppress initiated by rachel. New scan-run created: 5265432125.

devops-ci: Applying a temporary grant for svc-scanner-v2 now (60 minutes). Posting IAM change link: https://iam.internal/changes/3821

oliver: RBAC PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra-config/pull/2134 13 includes policy addition for svc-scanner-v2 -> kms:Decrypt on keystore-prod; description includes audit req_ids zz9a1/zz9a2.

sec-scan-bot: Re-run completed. Finding GSA-21077 is now visible, stack trace attached. Severity: HIGH. Evidence: shows unparameterized query in 1 place.

rachel: Good. Michael (security reviewer) can you take the remediation? If true positive: patch to parameterized query + unit test + deploy. Also add rule change: auto-noise-heuristic must never auto-suppress if metadata contains attempted-keystore-fetch=failed.

sam: I'll draft the rule change and open a follow-up PR against the scanner heuristics repo. Quick patch: change suppression predicate to require keystore fetch success or explicit human-signed audit proof.

oliver: Noted. One more ask: add a monitoring alert to detect repeated scanner 403s within a 1-hour window and page infra-oncall if frequency > 3.

rachel: Adding that to SEC-443. Closing loop: RBAC PR (#2134) open, unsuppress+re-run done, temporary grant applied and removed after 60m, scanner rule PR pending. We'll do a 1-paragraph incident note in security-ops after remediation.

sam: Thanks team. Small retrospective: when rotating principals, we need a checklist item: update scanner identity references and verify keystore access before next nightly run. I'll add it to the oncall runbook.

oliver: postmortem stub: root cause = principal rotation without scanner propagation; impact = 7 suppressed high-severity findings; remediation = RBAC fix + scanner rule change + monitoring + runbook update.

rachel: I'll keep SEC-443 open until PRs merge and tests confirm. If anything else pops up, ping here. :white_check_mark:
